title: Derived global Hom topology comparison for finite-field constructible models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers put
$$C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega):f(P)\subset E'\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E'\subset\Omega\},\qquad B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$$
[sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Let $c:C\to B$ be inclusion. For a scheme $V$ over $X$ set $C_V=p_V^*C$, $B_V=p_V^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and for a finite intermediate field $D\subset\Omega$ put $A_{D,V}=p_V^*C(-,D)$, with its restricted norm topology [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Work on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with K-flat derived scalar extension and unit $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars].

Fix a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$, put $A=A_{E,X}$, and let $K,N\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$ be bounded constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Define $S_R(V)=R_X\otimes_A^L V$ for $R=C,B$, $J=B_X\otimes_{C_X}^L(-)$, and $D=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,N)$ using the relative tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Then $D$ is bounded constructible in both the finite constant local model and stratified local-finite-presentation senses [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Also, for every small filtered diagram $(V_i^\bullet)$ of $A$-module complexes with one common termwise lower bound, the evaluation map
$$\varinjlim_i R\mathcal Hom_A(K,V_i^\bullet)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\varinjlim_iV_i^\bullet)$$
is invertible; these are exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

For each $R=C,B$ the evaluation transpose
$$\phi_R:S_RD\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{R_X}(S_RK,S_RN)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$, natural in $K,N$. Its transpose is exactly
$$S_RD\otimes^L_{R_X}S_RK\simeq R_X\otimes_A^L(D\otimes_A^L K)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mathrm{ev}}S_RN,$$
with K-flat balanced-tensor reassociation. Define $m_D:\operatorname{Res}_{A\to C_X}S_CD\to\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_X}S_BD$ by $z\otimes v\mapsto c_X(z)\otimes v$. On forgetting coefficients, $R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},m_D)$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of abelian groups [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

Let $\Psi_{K,N}$ be the actual morphism of derived global Hom objects induced by $J$, using the canonical reassociations $JS_CK\simeq S_BK$ and $JS_CN\simeq S_BN$:
$$\Psi_{K,N}:R\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_{C_X}(S_CK,S_CN)\longrightarrow R\Gamma R\mathcal Hom_{B_X}(S_BK,S_BN).$$
Under $R\Gamma\phi_C$ and $R\Gamma\phi_B$ it equals $R\Gamma(m_D)$; in particular $\Psi_{K,N}$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of abelian groups. The scalar-extended evaluation transposes are both $B_X\otimes_A^L(D\otimes_A^L K)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mathrm{ev}}S_BN$. All maps are natural in arrows of $K,N$. Derived global sections before and after restriction from $R_X$ to $A$ are canonically identified in this assertion. The same identifications hold in the section-ring model under the underlying-sheaf-preserving module equivalence. No site-perfectness, flatness of $c_X$, completeness of $\Omega$, or bound on the cohomological dimension of $k$ is imposed.

proof.text: First identify internal modules with section-ring module sheaves by the underlying-sheaf-preserving equivalence. The tensor comparison identifies exactness, K-flatness and the total tensor complexes, and the Hom comparison identifies derived internal Hom together with evaluation. For a coefficient map, extension of scalars is the same balanced coequalizer in the two presentations: the two action relations are identical after the section-action equivalence. Thus the comparison on scalar extensions is the identity on local tensors and remains so on K-flat representatives. Restriction of scalars also has identical underlying sheaves and actions in the two presentations. We may perform the following argument with section rings; transporting back preserves each of its specified maps, not only the objects.

source.place: Internal Hom, evaluation and K-flat tensor comparison; agent use of the existing internal-to-section comparison statements (Tags 08J9, 08JA).

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0$ and $(1)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma applies to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply the adic constructibility-predicate comparison to the finite normed field $E$. It carries the given finite constant local model conditions on $K,N$ to the stratified local-finite-presentation conditions. The $\underline E$ case of the small-coefficient internal-Hom finiteness theorem therefore makes $D=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,N)$ bounded constructible in that latter sense. Applying the predicate comparison in the reverse direction gives the finite constant local model condition on $D$. Here $E$ is a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $X$ is separated of finite type over a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, exactly as required; no condition on the cohomological dimension of $k$ enters.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 (preservation of constructibility by ambient Hom), using the existing small-coefficient finiteness and predicate-comparison statements.

proof.text: Apply constructible internal-Hom continuity with coefficient $\Lambda=\underline E$, source $K$, and the diagram $(V_i^\bullet)$ in the question. The Noetherian hypothesis was verified in step 2. The diagram is small and has the required common termwise lower bound; its terms need not be constructible. The comparison furnished by that statement is precisely the evaluation-induced map, represented by exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial representatives. Consequently it proves the requested continuity assertion with its stated convention on representatives.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Lemma 6.3.14; the cited existing node states the needed internal-sheaf continuity formulation explicitly.

proof.text: Apply the finite-subextension coefficient comparison with $S=A$, $T=C_X$, and $L=N$. The continuity hypothesis is step 3 and the cohomological lower bound is implied by boundedness of $N$. The ring $C$ is exactly the finite-subextension-valued coefficient ring of that comparison, rather than the norm-continuous ring $B$. It gives the isomorphism $\phi_C$. Its statement specifies its transpose by scalar-extended evaluation and K-flat balanced reassociation, and includes naturality in both inputs. The finite fields containing $E$ form the cofinal tail used there; no completeness of $\Omega$ is needed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15, with the existing evaluation-normalized coefficient-union comparison.

proof.text: Apply norm-algebraic-closure internal-Hom base change to the same $E,X,K,N$. Its rings $C,B$ and map $c$ are exactly those in the question, and its constructibility convention is the finite constant local model convention. It supplies $\phi_B$ as an isomorphism natural in both inputs, with the displayed evaluation transpose and K-flat reassociation. This is a distinct input from step 4: it does not identify $B$ with the union of finite-subextension coefficient rings and does not assume flatness of $c_X$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), existing agent obligation for norm-continuous coefficient internal-Hom comparison; no direct literature theorem for this topology comparison is claimed.

proof.text: Apply norm-algebraic-closure cohomology topology comparison to $V=D$, which meets its finite constant local model and boundedness hypotheses by step 2. It says that $R\Gamma(m_D)$ is invertible after forgetting coefficients, for the actual map represented by $z\otimes d\mapsto c_X(z)\otimes d$. Use derived-sections scalar coherence for $A\to C_X$ and $A\to B_X$ to identify derived sections before and after restriction. These are natural identifications in the ordinary unbounded categories and require neither flat restriction nor preservation of injectives by restriction. Thus the global isomorphism is the one in the question.

source.place: Paragraph (3), existing global coefficient-topology comparison; scalar-forgetting coherence is Stacks Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition).

proof.text:
Write $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_{R_X}(S_RK,S_RN)$. The strong monoidal composition comparisons identify $JS_CV$ with $S_BV$ for $V=D,K,N$, including the scalar units. Let $\chi:JH_C\to H_B$ be the transpose of $J(\mathrm{ev}_C)$, and let $\theta:H_C\to\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}H_B$ be its composite with the scalar unit. By the normalized scalar-Hom adjunction, transpose computations may be made after inserting $S_CK\to\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}JS_CK$. Under $JS_CD\simeq S_BD$, the transpose of $\chi\circ J\phi_C$ is
$$B_X\otimes_A^L(D\otimes_A^L K)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mathrm{ev}}S_BN.$$
Indeed $\phi_C$ is by definition the transpose of $C_X\otimes_A^L\mathrm{ev}$, and the monoidal composition comparison takes its scalar extension to $B_X\otimes_A^L\mathrm{ev}$. This is also the transpose of $\phi_B$, so uniqueness in the tensor-Hom adjunction gives $\chi\circ J\phi_C=\phi_B$. Naturality of the scalar unit now gives
$$\theta\circ\phi_C=\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}(\phi_B)\circ m_D^C,$$
where $m_D^C:S_CD\to\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}S_BD$ is the $C_X$-linear map whose underlying $A$-linear map is $m_D$. Its formula is $z\otimes d\mapsto c_X(z)\otimes d$: it is the unit $S_CD\to\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}JS_CD$ followed by reassociation. This proves the required equality of maps by adjunction and its unit, without any faithfulness claim for scalar extension.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 0D6D: monoidality and scalar-composition reassociation; agent formal transpose calculation from the cited normalized comparisons.

proof.text:
By definition the map on derived global Hom objects induced by $J$ is $R\Gamma(\theta)$, with the scalar-forgetting identifications of step 6: it applies the strong monoidal functor $J$ to evaluation and inserts its scalar unit. Applying $R\Gamma$ to the equality in step 7 yields
$$\Psi_{K,N}\circ R\Gamma(\phi_C)=R\Gamma(\phi_B)\circ R\Gamma(m_D).$$
Both $R\Gamma(\phi_R)$ are invertible by steps 4 and 5, and $R\Gamma(m_D)$ is invertible by step 6, so $\Psi_{K,N}$ is invertible. Each equality in step 7 is natural under precomposition in $K$ and postcomposition in $N$: evaluation has these naturalities, and transposition, scalar units and the cited monoidal comparisons are natural. The same is true after derived sections by scalar coherence. Step 1 identifies every evaluation and scalar unit in the section-ring presentation, so the identical square and both scalar-extended evaluation transposes hold there as well.
